name: Azariah
source_summary: A prophet, son of Oded, whose Spirit-inspired message to King Asa -- that the LORD would be found by those who sought Him -- prompted a sweeping national reform, removing idols and restoring the altar of the LORD in Judah.
family_friendly_summary: After King Asa won a great battle with God's help, a prophet named Azariah met him with an important message from God. Azariah told Asa that God would stay close to him and his people as long as they kept seeking God -- but warned that turning away from God brought trouble, the way Israel had suffered when it had no true worship and no teaching about God's law. Azariah encouraged Asa to be strong and not give up, promising that his faithful work would be rewarded. Asa took the message to heart. He removed the idols from his kingdom and repaired the altar of the LORD, leading his whole nation back to worshiping God.
adult_story: Azariah, son of Oded, was a prophet whom the Spirit of God moved to meet King Asa of Judah after Asa's victory over a massive Cushite invasion (2 Chronicles 14:9-15; 15:1-2). His message was direct: "The LORD is with you when you are with Him. And if you seek Him, He will let you find Him; but if you forsake Him, He will forsake you" (15:2). Azariah reminded Asa of Israel's earlier history -- long stretches "without the true God, without a teaching priest and without law," a time of national distress and violence that only ended when the people, in their trouble, turned back and sought the LORD (15:3-6). He closed with an exhortation: "be strong and do not lose courage, for there is reward for your work" (15:7). Asa did not merely hear the prophecy -- he acted on it. He removed the detestable idols from Judah, Benjamin, and the towns he had captured in Ephraim, restored the altar of the LORD in front of the temple porch, and led the nation in a covenant renewal, gathering the people to sacrifice to the LORD with all their heart and soul (15:8-15). The chapter closes noting that Judah had peace for the rest of that period, tracing the reform directly back to a single prophetic word spoken by a man who otherwise appears nowhere else in Scripture.

devotionals: Azariah promised Asa that God is found by those who seek Him, and Asa's reform proved it. God is found that way by anyone seeking Him through Jesus.
Azariah warned that forsaking God brings distress, but seeking Him brings reward for the work of faith. Jesus is the reward waiting for everyone who seeks after God.
